record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Is there a natural integer p such that 2-abelian-squares of period at least p can be avoided over a binary alphabet?

evidence.quote: Is there a natural integer p such that 2-abelian-squares of period at least p can be avoided over a binary alphabet?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma = \{0,1\}$ be the binary alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. For a word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n \in \Sigma^*$ and an integer $k \geq 1$, the $k$-abelian equivalence relation $\sim_k$ on $\Sigma^*$ is defined by: $u \sim_k v$ if and only if, for every word $x \in \Sigma^*$ with $|x| \leq k$, the number of occurrences of $x$ as a (contiguous) factor of $u$ equals the number of occurrences of $x$ as a factor of $v$ (in particular, $|u| = |v|$). 

A non-empty word $w$ is called a $k$-abelian square if $w = uv$ with $|u| = |v|$ and $u \sim_k v$. The period of such a $k$-abelian square $w = uv$ is the integer $|u|$. An infinite word $\mathbf{w} \in \Sigma^{\mathbb{N}}$ is said to avoid $2$-abelian squares of period at least $p$ if no factor of $\mathbf{w}$ is a $2$-abelian square whose period is $\geq p$.

Question: Does there exist a positive integer $p$ such that there exists an infinite binary word $\mathbf{w} \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ avoiding all $2$-abelian squares of period at least $p$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether 2-abelian squares of period at least some integer p can be avoided over a binary alphabet appears in the literature on avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions and is repeatedly cited as an open problem. While related results are known (e.g., 3-abelian cubes and 5-abelian cubes are avoidable on binary alphabets), no construction or impossibility proof for the binary 2-abelian-square version with bounded period appears to have been published.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies avoidability of k-abelian repetitions of bounded period on small alphabets; the binary 2-abelian square case with period bound is left open.
status_evidence.claim: Question is mentioned in the avoidability literature without resolution.

status_evidence.title: 5-Abelian cubes are avoidable on binary alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Construction avoiding 5-abelian cubes on binary alphabets; analogous binary 2-abelian-square question with period bound remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Related binary k-abelian repetition results exist but not for 2-abelian squares with period at least p.
